Energia Rates and Tariffs
Compare Energia’s latest electricity and gas rates across smart meter, EV, dual fuel and standard tariffs, with clear unit-rate and standing-charge breakdowns that help you cut through the small print and see what you’ll actually pay.

compare Energia electricity plans
to find the best option for your home.

Microgeneration
Microgeneration rates
Microgeneration
is the process of producing your own electricity at home, typically using renewable sources such as
solar panels
. If you generate excess electricity, you may be eligible to receive credit for exporting energy back to the grid. These payments are usually applied as a credit on your electricity bill and can help reduce overall energy costs.
View microgeneration rates
FAQs About energy rates Ireland:
What are Energia electricity peak, day and night times?
Night and peak electricity times depend on the type of meter you have.
If you have a Smart meter, it automatically adjusts for daylight savings. Your night rate runs from 11pm to 8am all year round.
If you have an MCC02 meter, it doesn’t adjust for daylight savings. So:
From late March to late October, night rate is from 12am to 9am
From late October to late March, it goes back to 11pm to 8am
If you have an MCC12 meter, your peak time is between 5pm to 7pm.
Does Energia offer different tariffs for day/night meters?
Yes, Energia offers different tariffs for day/night meters. We provide specific plans such as the
Smart Day/Night tariff
, which features two time bands with cheaper night rates, allowing customers to save by using electricity during off-peak hours.
What is a unit rate (kWh)?
A unit rate is the cost per kilowatt hour (kWh) of electricity or gas you use. It’s the main variable cost on your energy bill.
What is a standing charge?
A standing charge is a fixed daily cost for maintaining your connection to the energy network, regardless of usage.
What is the difference between smart meter and standard tariffs?
Smart tariffs use time-based pricing (day, night, peak), while standard tariffs use either a single 24-hour rate or a day/night structure.

FAQs about our Electricity Price Plans:
How do I compare electricity plans in Ireland?
Compare the unit rate, standing charge,
average electricity bill
, discount, contract length and whether the plan suits your meter type and usage habits.
How long is the Energia electricity contract?
Energia electricity contracts are available for either 12 or 24 months. If you end your contract early (before the 12-month period is up), a termination fee will apply. See our full
terms and conditions
for more details.
What times are night and peak rate electricity charged?
Night and peak rate times depend on your meter type and tariff. For smart meters, the night rate is usually 11pm to 8am all year round and adjusts automatically for daylight savings. For MCC02 day/night meters, the night rate is 12am to 9am from late March to late October and 11pm to 8am from late October to late March. For MCC12 smart data meters, the peak rate is usually 5pm to 7pm. Shifting electricity use to off-peak or night-rate hours may help reduce your costs. Learn more about how a
time-of-use tariff
works.
I am elderly and worried about my power supply being disconnected in winter. What can I do?
If you’re aged 66 or over, you can
register as a Vulnerable Customer
. Once registered, you’ll be added to the Special Services Register, which protects you from electricity or gas disconnection during winter months, from 1st November to 31st March.
Ready to switch?
The quickest way to switch to Energia is online. However, if you prefer to speak with an advisor or need assistance, you can request a call back, and one of our experts will contact you at a time that suits you best.

Energy bills can be confusing..
But we’re here to help break it down for you with this short guide to the key information that is included on your bill and what it means for you and your home.
What is a utility bill?
A utility bill is a statement that shows how much you owe for essential services such as electricity or gas. It includes details of your energy usage over a set period, along with charges, taxes, and any applicable discounts. Your Energia bill is a type of utility bill, showing exactly how much energy your home has used and how your final cost is calculated.
How your bill is calculated:
Your electricity or gas meter records the amount of energy your home has used. ESB Networks or Gas Networks Ireland will read your meter four times per year and share the readings with us to calculate your bill. Outside of these times, we may ask you to provide us with a meter reading to ensure your bill is kept accurate and to avoid estimate readings. Your actual bill will vary depending on your usage, tariff and meter type. You can compare your costs with the
average electricity bill in Ireland
and learn how annual energy costs are estimated.
If you have a Smart Meter your meter readings will be automatically sent to the network operators and shared with us to calculate your bill. Please note, depending on your CTF status, bills may be estimated.
How you will be billed:
If you have registered for an Energia online account, you will receive your bill online. We will email you to let you know when you have new bill available to view and you can simply log into your online account either on web or via our free smartphone app, to see your latest bill, account balance and the option to download a copy of your bill (and any bill within your account, up to two years).
If you have not yet registered for an Energia online account, you will receive your bills by post.
Your electricity & gas bills:
Electricity and gas are billed separately so, if you’re a Dual Fuel customer, you will receive two separate bills one for electricity and one for gas and each will be paid separately. These bills may not arrive together at the same time and this is normal, don’t worry.

Understanding Your Bill
Energia is a member of EAI: Electricity Association of Ireland and we are pleased to support the launch of a new Energy Bill Guide to help customers feel more confident about their electricity bills and everyday energy use.
The guide explains how bills are put together and helps customers to better understand the impact of how and when they use electricity, including the role smart meters can play.

What to look for on your bill
Page 1:
In the top right-hand corner, you will find most of the key account information which includes:
1. Your account number:
This is your Energia account number which identifies your electricity or gas account. You may wish to make note of this number as it will be required should you need to contact us or if you would like to register for an Energia online account.
2. Your MPRN or GPRN:
Your MPRN (Meter Point Reference Number) of GPRN (Gas Meter Point Reference Number) identifies your meter connection with ESB Network or Gas Networks Ireland and these numbers will be unique to your home.
3. Billing period and due date:
Your billing period dates relate to the timeframe of the electricity usage you are being billed for. The due date is the date which you must pay your bill by.
If you are a Level Pay customer, you don’t need to take any action as the cost of your bills will be covered within your monthly direct debit payments which are collected automatically on the due date indicated on your bill.

Billing FAQs
Accessing and managing bills
Can I pay my bill online?
Yes, you can pay your bill online through your Energia online account.
Why register for Energy Online?
You get 24/7 access to view your bills and make payments conveniently.
You can use our
Fast Pay service
to make advance payments towards your energy bills.
All payments are secure and easy to manage.

Can I get my bill online instead of by post?
Yes, you can choose to receive your Energia bill online.
Simply register for our Energy Online service, and your bills will be:
Emailed directly to you
Available to view anytime through your online account
This option is secure, convenient, and helps you manage your bills more easily, while also reducing paper waste. You may also be eligible for a discount of 4% on your bill if you choose to receive your bill online.
Register for Energy Online here
What payment options does Energia Provide?
We offer a range of payment options to suit different needs and help you manage your energy bills with ease:
1. Direct Debit
The full bill amount is automatically taken from your bank account 14 days after your bill is issued.
It’s a hassle-free way to stay on top of payments and you may be eligible for discounts when you choose this option.
2. FastPay
A quick and easy way to make debit or credit card payments online.
You can add credit to your account, which will be deducted from your next bill.
Great for building up credit.
3. Level Pay
Spread your estimated annual energy costs evenly over 12 monthly payments.
Monthly payments are calculated based on consumption and we review at least once a year and encourage customers to regularly log in to their online account to review bills.
We will notify you in advance of any changes to your monthly payment.
When do I have to pay my bill?
The Payment Due Date is indicated on the top of the bill. This is generally 14 days after the bill is issued.
Will I receive one bill for both electricity and gas?
If you're a Dual Fuel customer with Energia, you'll receive two separate bills, one for electricity and one for gas.
Here’s why:
Electricity and gas are billed separately, based on the meter reading schedules of ESB Networks (electricity) and Gas Networks Ireland (gas).
Your bills may be issued on different dates, and each payment will be processed separately.
Do Energia accept Social Welfare payments?
The Social Welfare can’t pay Energia directly, but you can organise for them to make payment directly to you. You will need to make Social Welfare aware when you change supplier.
How can I reduce my bills?
There are a few simple ways to lower your energy bills:
1. Choose the right payment options
You can get discounts by paying your bill through Direct Debit or by signing up for online billing.
2. Check your energy plan
Make sure you're on a plan that suits your needs. If you're not sure, we can help you review your options. Call our customer support line at
0818 405 405
to review your options.
3. Use less energy at home
Small changes can make a big difference. We’ve put together an Energy Efficiency Tips Guide with practical ideas to help you save energy and money.
Visit our
Energy Efficiency Tips Guide
to get started.

Bill understanding and calculation
How is my bill calculated?
Your Energia bill is based on how much electricity or gas you use. Here’s a simple breakdown of how we calculate it:
1. Reading your meter:
We measure your energy use in units from your electricity and/or gas meter. ESB Networks (for electricity) and Gas Networks Ireland (for gas) read your meter about four times a year.
If a recent reading isn’t available, we’ll use an estimated reading based on your previous usage.
Or you can send us your own meter reading  through your
Energy Online account
to make your bill more accurate.
2. Working out your usage
We look at the meter readings at the start and end of your billing period to see how much energy you used.
If our prices changed during that time, we split your usage:
- Units used before the change are charged at the old price.
- Units used after the change are charged at the new price.
3. Your plan (tariff)
We multiply the number of units you used by the price per unit in your energy plan.
4. Other charges on your bill also includes:
A daily standing charge (a fixed cost)
VAT (Value Added Tax)
Government charges like:
- The PSO Levy (for electricity)
- Carbon Tax (for gas)

Check out our
Understanding Your Energia Bill Guide
My bill looks complicated – can you help me understand it?
Absolutely, we know your Energia bill might look a little different from what you're used to, and we're here to help. To make things easier, we’ve created a simple guide that explains each part of your bill in plain language.
View our
Understanding Your Bill Guide here
What are Unit Rates?
Unit rates are the price you pay for each unit of energy you use. Energy is measured in kilowatt-hours (kWh), that’s the amount of electricity used to power things like lights, appliances or heating. Each kWh you use is called a unit.
To work out your energy cost, we multiply:
-The number of units you’ve used
- By the price per unit in your plan (your unit rate)
You’ll see your unit rates clearly listed on your bill, so you can understand how your charges are calculated.
What if I am a multi-rate customer?
If your electricity plan includes different rates for different times of day (like Day, Night or Peak hours), your bill will still look the same as usual. However, if our prices change, you’ll see an extra line on your bill for each rate. This shows the new price per unit for that time period.
What is a standing charge?
A standing charge is a daily fee that helps cover the cost of keeping your home connected to the energy grid.
The fee helps cover the costs of services like:
Meter reading
Network maintenance
Operating costs for supplying energy to your home
This charge is applied to your bill as a daily rate, and the total amount depends on the length of your billing period, usually around 60 days, though this can vary slightly. We include this charge to ensure your energy supply is reliable and well-maintained.
What is the PSO Levy?
The PSO (Public Service Obligation) levy is a charge set by the Irish Government and applied to all electricity customers in Ireland.
It helps support the generation of electricity from:
Renewable sources (like wind and solar)
Sustainable and indigenous sources (produced within Ireland)
The levy is reviewed and set each year by the Commission for Regulation of Utilities (CRU) and appears as a separate item on your electricity bill. In some cases, the levy may be negative, meaning you’ll receive a credit on your bill instead of a charge.
Why is there an adjustment on my bill?
Sometimes we will have to add an adjustment to your bill, these adjustments should be labelled to explain what the adjustment relates to, or you may have received an email in advance. If you ever need clarification on any adjustments, please contact us on

ESBN
replacement data adjustment’ this will show what additional credits or debits we need to apply to your bill. This could be related to poor connectivity or storm outages.
In addition,
ESBN

No, the team are trying to contact you to give you an update on your account with Energia. The sooner we speak to you, the sooner we can help you with your account, or overdue balance

I have received a letter from your Payment and Accounts Resolutions Team, what does this mean?
The Payment and Accounts Resolutions Team is part of our Customer Experience team. If you’ve received a letter from them, it’s important not to ignore it.
What the letter means:
•It explains why we’re getting in touch, this could be about a query on your account or an overdue payment.
•It includes contact details so you can speak to us by phone or email.
Please reach out to the team as soon as possible. We’re here to help and will work with you to resolve any issues.
Can the Payment and Accounts Resolutions Team disconnect my supply if I don't pay my bills?
Yes, your electricity or gas supply can be disconnected if bills are not paid and payment terms are not followed. But this is always a last resort.
What you need to know:
Disconnection only happens when all other options have been exhausted.
The team will make every effort to contact you and help you avoid this.
The sooner you get in touch, the sooner we can work with you to find a solution.
How can a Pre-payment Meter help me with my account if I am behind in my bills and payments?
If you're finding it hard to keep up with your energy bills, a pre-payment meter (PPM) can help you manage your account more easily. It lets you pay for your electricity and gas as you use it, which can make budgeting simpler.
Here’s how it works
:
We’ll move your current account balance onto the pre-payment meter.
Each time you top up, 10% goes towards paying off your balance, and 90% goes towards your energy use.
If you rent your home, we’ll need your landlord’s permission before installing a
PPM
. We’ll also check that your current meter is compatible for a
PPM
.

FAQs about our Dual Fuel Plans & Offers
What is a dual fuel tariff?
A dual fuel tariff (also called a dual fuel bundle or plan) means your energy supplier provides both your gas and electricity.
This type of tariff offers:
Convenience: one supplier
Potential savings: compared to having separate tariffs
Flexible options: Energia offers plans for both standard and smart meters
You can choose a dual fuel plan that suits your home and helps you manage your energy more efficiently.
How do I switch dual fuel providers?
Switching to Energia for both gas and electricity is quick and easy. It takes around 4 minutes to complete the process online.
Here’s what you’ll need:
Your
MPRN
(for electricity) and
GPRN
(for gas) – both are on your current bill
Recent meter readings ( where required )
Your bank details
Once you sign up, we’ll contact your current supplier and manage the switch for you. There’s no need to get in touch with them yourself, and your energy supply won’t be interrupted.
For new users, our
new customer guide
explains how our energy plans work and what to expect on your first bill.
Is Energia a green energy supplier?
Yes Energia provides 100% Green Electricity and supplies approximately 20% of Ireland’s total wind power.*
We were also chosen as winners of the Green Energy Provider Award at the Green Energy Awards in 2020.
*
Subject to verification by the CRU under the CRU’s Green Source Product Verification process.
How can I save money on gas and electricity bills?
There are lots of ways to save money on your energy bills with Energia.
Quick savings:
Get up to 10%* off your bills by setting up Direct Debit (6%) and switching to Online Billing (4%). It’s a simple way to save while making your payments easier and more eco-friendly.
Call us on
0818 405 405
to switch to Direct Debit and Online Billing.
You can also save money and cut costs by making small changes at home like:
Using LED bulbs
Turning off devices when not in use
Heating only the rooms you need
Keeping your boiler serviced
Using smart thermostats to control heating more efficiently
See our full
list of energy saving tips
to start saving today.
* Discounts apply to selected plans only and may vary by tariff!
Ready to switch?
The quickest way to switch to Energia is online. However, if you prefer to speak with an advisor or need assistance, you can request a call back, and one of our experts will contact you at a time that suits you best.
Request a call back
Switch now

Your Privacy
When you visit any website, it may store or retrieve information on your browser, mostly in the form of cookies. This information might be about you, your preferences, or your device, and is mostly used to make the site work as you expect. The information does not usually identify you directly, but it can give you a more personalized web experience. Because we respect your right to privacy, you can choose not to allow some types of cookies. Click on the different category headings to learn more and change our default settings. Frequently asked questions:
Is it easy to switch gas providers in Ireland?
Yes, switching to an Energia gas plan is quick and easy. You can register yourself online or if you prefer to chat with someone, you can call our sales team on
0818 300 701
. It takes around 4 minutes to complete the process online.
Here’s what you’ll need:
Your
GPRN
(found on your gas bill)
A current gas meter reading
Your bank details
Once you sign up, we’ll contact your old gas supplier and take care of the switch. There’s no need to contact them yourself, and your gas supply won’t be interrupted.
Switch to an
Energia gas plan online here
today.
Energy rates
Our gas plans have different rates depending on the products. Discover the full breakdown on our dedicated
Tariff Rates page
.
When switching to Energia do I need to contact my previous gas provider?
No you do not have to contact your previous provider, we will do that without any disruption to your gas supply.
How can I save money on gas?
There are several ways to reduce your gas bill like:
Switching to direct debit and online billing: Get up to 10%
*
off your gas bills by setting up Direct Debit (6%) and switching to Online Billing (4%)
Using your heating wisely: lower the thermostat, heat only the rooms you need, and use timers
Keeping your boiler in good shape: regular servicing helps it run efficiently
Upgrading your home:
Energia’s Cosy Homes Scheme
offers
SEAI
grants for insulation and heating improvements
See more
tips on lowering your gas bill here
.
* Discounts apply to selected plans only and may vary by tariff!
Who supplies Ireland with gas?
Ireland’s natural gas comes from two main sources:
Imports from Scotland via pipeline
Domestic production from the Corrib gas fields
As the Corrib supply decreases, Ireland is expected to rely more heavily on imports, around 80% by the mid-2020s, rising to over 90% by 2030.
How to read a gas meter in Ireland?
Your gas meter is read four times a year by someone from Gas Networks Ireland (GNI), and the readings are sent to Energia to help calculate your bill.
Because Energia bills customers six times a year, the other two bills are based on estimated readings using your previous usage.
To make sure your bill is accurate, you can submit your own gas meter reading through your
online Energia account
.
You can learn how to
read your gas meter with our step-by-step guide
.
Ready to switch?
The quickest way to switch to Energia is online. However, if you prefer to speak with an advisor or need assistance, you can request a call back, and one of our experts will contact you at a time that suits you best.
Request a call back
Switch now
Faults & Emergencies
If you are having difficulty with your energy supply or smell gas please call us using our
fault and emergency contact numbers
.

FAQs
Are smart meter plans worth it?
Smart meter plans are generally worth it as they offer several benefits. With a smart meter, you get accurate billing based on real-time energy usage, eliminating estimated bills. You can monitor and manage your consumption more effectively, often saving money by using electricity during off-peak hours with tailored tariffs like day/night or EV Smart Drive plans.
What is the downside of a smart meter?
Smart meters do have a few downsides to consider. Once installed, you can’t switch back to a traditional meter. Also, in some rural areas, weak signal strength can affect automatic readings, so you might need to submit readings manually now and then.
I have a day/night meter, can I get a smart meter?
Yes, you can upgrade to a smart meter even if you currently have a day/night meter. Once you choose your preferred plan, you can complete the switch online. If you opt for a smart meter plan, we will contact you within a few days to move forward with your application.
What are the off-peak times for smart meters?
For most Energia smart plans, off-peak hours are between 11pm and 8am. Some plans also include ultra-low-cost charging windows, such as 2am–6am for EV charging.
I have a day/night meter, can I get a smart meter?
Yes, you can upgrade to a smart meter even if you currently have a day/night meter.
Ready to switch?
The quickest way to switch to Energia is online. However, if you prefer to speak with an advisor or need assistance, you can request a call back, and one of our experts will contact you at a time that suits you best.

A Guide to Switch to Energia
Everything you need to know when switching to cheaper, greener and smarter energy
View plans
What you need to switch
Before you get started, make sure you have a few key details ready. This will help make the process quick and hassle-free.
MPRN (Electricity)
or
GPRN (Gas)
. You can find this on your latest bill.
Bank Details.
You will need these to set up a direct debit.
Address and Eircode.
You will need this to confirm your energy connection.
Meter Readings.
Some switches may need a current meter reading.
Request a call back
Switch Now
Switching to Energia is easy.
Follow these steps to get a great deal, top service and smart customer solutions that save money, time and energy.
3 simple steps to switch:
Step 1 - Choose your new energy plan
Compare our best price energy plans and find the best deal for your home
View all plans
Step 2 - Complete your switch online
Switch to Energia in as little as four minutes when you switch online
Switch to Energia
Step 3 - Sit back and relax
Our customer service team will take care of everything else
Get in touch
Ready to switch to Energia?
Switch online
View Energy Plans
Call Us
0818 300 701
Request a Call-Back
Contact Us
I've switched to Energia, what happens next?
Once you have completed your gas or electric switch online or by phone our team will take care of everything.
We'll contact your previous energy supplier to let them know you’re switching to Energia.
We'll send you a registration letter confirming your details, the plan and prices you’ve signed up for with Energia. You will have a 14 day cooling off period if you change your mind.
We'll issue your Energia Welcome pack which contains your new Energia account number and helpful information to get your started.
We'll pass on your meter reading to your old supplier and they will send you a final bill.
A new account will be opened and your existing account with your previous supplier will be closed.
We'll issue your first Energia bill approximately 8-10 weeks after your switch (the date will depend on your meter reading window) and after this you will receive a bill bi-monthly.
Estimated reads may not be accurate due to the absence of historic usage information which may impact billing.
Any existing arrears on your account will be dealt with by your previous supplier.
There will be no interruption to your gas and electric supply when you switch as there is no change to your meter at this time.

Look at more than just price

What else is important to you as a customer? Green energy, smart products, quality customer service or customer rewards? The best overall value might come from more than just simply the price you pay.

When you visit any website, it may store or retrieve information on your browser, mostly in the form of cookies. The information does not usually identify you directly, but it can give you a more personalized web experience. Because we respect your right to privacy, you can choose not to allow some types of cookies. Click on the different category headings to learn more and change our default settings. Your guide to smart meters
View all plans
What are the benefits of a Smart Meter Plan?
Accurate billing
Reconfigured smart meters on MCC12 can send readings automatically if it has good connectivity, helping billing accuracy. If you have an MCC16 meter or an unreconfigured smart meter, you’ll still need to send readings.
Smart tariffs
Smart meters enable access to smart tariffs, saving you money by using electricity during cheaper, off-peak times.
Reduce costs
By switching to a smart tariff, you can track your energy use, adjust your habits, cut electricity consumption, and save money.
Reduce carbon footprint
With an ever-growing population and more people using electricity at peak times, making small changes can help reduce your carbon footprint.
Export and earn
If you generate solar or wind energy, smart meters accurately measure exported surplus energy making sure you're paid correctly.
Freedom to move
It's completely free to get a smart meter installed in your home - simply contact
ESB
Networks to register your interest.
What Smart Plan is best for me?
We have a number of smart plans available for you to choose from.
View Smart Plans
What are Smart Meters?
Smart meters are an upgrade from traditional meters. Traditional meters require manual readings and often lead to estimated bills. Smart meters give you more accurate information on your energy usage using digital technology – this can help you to manage your consumption, become more efficient and reduce your bills.
If you don’t currently have a smart meter, ESB Networks will notify you when they are installing in your area. You can also request one through ESB Networks below.
Request a smart meter
How do Smart Meters work?
Smart meters work by using technology that enables them to communicate remotely with your supplier, providing periodic data on energy usage. This will allow you to view and manage your usage more easily allowing you to find ways to save.
Depending on the connection, your meter can collect data on your energy consumption every 30 minutes which will be sent to your supplier either daily or bi-monthly. This data includes how much energy you are using and when you are using it.
How can Smart Meters benefit customers?
Smart meters could help you save money on your electricity bills. Typically, electricity companies charge different amounts depending on the various times of the day and how much pressure is on the electricity systems.
Monitoring your electricity usage in your Energy Online app using Energy Insights, you can have better control of your usage. Depending on which plan you choose, you can see if making simple changes can save you money on your bills.
Do I need to sign up to a smart plan?
If you have a smart meter, you will still need to opt in to a smart meter plan. We have a range of smart plans to suit your needs and lifestyle. Check out the link below to see which plan is smartest for you.
Please note: due to industry rules for smart metering, if you move to a smart tariff, it’s not possible to revert to a non-smart tariff or an old meter type.
Choose your plan

Your Privacy
When you visit any website, it may store or retrieve information on your browser, mostly in the form of cookies. This information might be about you, your preferences, or your device, and is mostly used to make the site work as you expect. The information does not usually identify you directly, but it can give you a more personalized web experience. Because we respect your right to privacy, you can choose not to allow some types of cookies. Click on the different category headings to learn more and change our default settings. Blocking some types of cookies may impact your experience of the site and the services we are able to offer.

These cookies are necessary for the website to function and cannot be switched off in our systems. You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the site will not then work. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable information.

These cookies allow us to count visits and traffic sources so we can measure and improve the performance of our site. They help us to know which pages are the most and least popular and see how visitors move around the site. All information these cookies collect is aggregated and therefore anonymous. If you do not allow these cookies we will not know when you have visited our site, and will not be able to monitor its performance.

All About Smart Meters
Electric Vehicle Plans & Chargers
Customer notice
We are increasing our residential Electricity and Gas prices from 12th October 2026.
Please see here for more information.
Energia Smart EV Plans - Where Smart Meets Driving
Discover our range of EV tariffs, products and services.
Smart EV charging is a type of charging that uses devices such as your phone and smart meter to communicate with the grid to optimise the charging process. The charging process is optimised based on things like the time of the day,
electricity prices
, and your EV battery percentage. Energia offers a range of EV plans, products and services. Check out
Energia’s EV tariff rates here
to better understand what suits your needs best.
Smart EV Electricity Tariffs
EV Smart Drive
EV Smart Drive plan is a 12-month contract with 100% renewable electricity offering longer charging windows, and the chance to charge your electric vehicle from 2am to 6am at a low rate of 9.42c/kWh.
Select EV Smart Drive Plan
EV Smart Drive Plus
The EV Smart Drive Plus plan is a 12-month contract with 100% renewable electricity offering low rates throughout the night with our more flexible EV tariff and 4hr charging window.
Select  EV Smart Drive Plus Plan
Home Charging Bundle
The Home Charging Bundle offers a free home charging point from Ohme or Zappi when you sign up to one of our EV tariffs through your car dealer.
Find out more
How does EV smart charging work?
Smart EV charging is a system in which an electric vehicle and a charger share a data connection, and the charger shares a data connection with a charging operator and an energy utility. When an electric vehicle is plugged in, the charger automatically transmits important data to the charging operator and energy utility, in order to optimise charging. Smart charging allows users to monitor, control and manage the charging process and energy usage remotely.
What are the advantages of signing up for a smart EV Plan?
There is a plethora of advantages when signing up for an EV plan. An EV plan, in addition to savings on fuel costs, can reduce your carbon footprint and contribute to a healthier environment, supporting Ireland’s acceleration to a greener, cleaner future, while also helping save you money. Signing up to Energia’s EV plan provide you with loads of benefits and helps save money.
Smart EV Dual Fuel Tariffs
EV Smart Drive Dual Fuel
Get our lowest EV charge rate of 9.42c/kWh with a 4hr charging window plus 10% off standard gas.
Choose a plan
EV Smart Drive Plus Dual Fuel
Get low rates throughout the night with our more flexible EV tariff and 4hr charging window plus 10% off standard gas.
Choose a plan
Compare EV tariffs
Want to explore all options before choosing? View our full range of
dual fuel plans
for Irish homes.
Hear from Our Happy Customers
See how our customers are benefiting from our EV offerings
The installation process for the EV charger was really straightforward. We just had to purchase the installation through the Energia site. We had the installation partner come out and do a site visit, completed the installation for us within four hours and we were able to charge our car.
Brian
EVCP and Smart Meter Plan customer
When I crunched the numbers, Energia was the plan that worked out best for us. The EV Smart Drive plan gives us a four-hour window overnight — 2am to 6am — at a discounted rate. During that time, that gives me the opportunity to charge my car and to set my appliances.
Michael
EV Smart Drive customer
01
02
Seamless charging at home and on the go
Need a home charging point?
Energia offers a range of EV home charging points and installation offers in the Energia Smart Home Store. Browse from the charging points available that come with unique features to ensure you find the exact charging point that works for you.
Get a home charge point
Fuel Savings Calculator
Did you know that the cost of running an electric car can be much lower than the cost of fuelling a petrol or diesel-powered vehicle. Our partner FASTER project has developed an EV Fuel Savings Calculator to show you the potential savings you could make if you switch to electric.
Open calculator
Find Your Nearest EV Charger in Ireland
Easily locate EV charging stations across Ireland with Zapmap. Plan your route, check charger availability, and get real-time updates.
View Zapmap
Support for wherever you are on your EV journey
No matter where you are on your EV journey, Energia is here to guide, offer advice and help you design an EV plan that saves you money but also helps you reduce your carbon footprint.
What EV grants are available?
EV grants reduce the upfront costs of buying an electric car, making it a possible choice for all individuals who are wanting to switch to electric. Visit our page for more information on Electric Car Grants.
View EV grants available
Check out our EV buyers guide
It is crucial to understand the procedures involved when switching to an electric vehicle.
The EV buyers guide will help you navigate the process of choosing, owning, and maintaining an electric vehicle in Ireland
View EV buyers guide
EV Charger Installation guide
Proper electric car charger installation requires the skills and tools. It is important you use a certified electrician to do the work for you.
See  EV Charger Installation guide
New EV Owner's Guide
Take a look through our guide for your EV journey. In this guide, we will walk you through the essential steps you should take after bringing home your electric vehicle.
Visit EV Owner's Guide
Energia EV plans FAQs
Do I need a smart charger for my EV?
Yes, Smart EV chargers need to be connected to WI-FI, in order for EVs to avail of their benefits. With some chargers using a simple plug and use system.
Do you need a smart meter for EV charging?
No, you do not need a smart meter for EV charging. But having a
smart meter
allows you to take advantage of the EV tariffs and lower overnight charging rates.
Should I charge my EV to 100% at home?
It is best to avoid charging your EV to 100% or letting the battery go below 20% regularly as this can lead to accelerated battery degradation.
What is smart charging EV energy?
Smart EV charging schedules your home EV charging for when it is most grid friendly and cheapest. The systems algorithm looks ahead 24 hours, taking into account your energy tariffs and estimated carbon intensity of the grid to select the best time to charge your vehicle.
Will charging an EV at my house double my electricity bill?
80% of the time electric vehicle owners charge their cars at home, which add up to about 3,000 kWh or more to your electricity bill.

Energia Microgeneration Rate and Guide
Get Paid for the Renewable Energy You Generate
Unlock the potential of your home or business to generate clean energy and earn with Energia's Microgeneration support. Energia currently offers a competitive rate of 18.5 cent (
18.5c/kWh
) for every unit of surplus electricity you export back to the grid.
What is Microgeneration and Feed-in Tariffs?
Microgeneration
is when you generate your own electricity using technologies such as
solar PV panels
or solar battery storage. During the day, your solar panels generate electricity that can be used in your home or business. If you generate more electricity than you use, the excess energy is automatically exported back to the electricity grid. The payment you receive for exporting this surplus electricity is commonly known as a feed-in tariff. In Ireland, this payment is officially provided through the Clean Export Guarantee (CEG).
Energia’s Microgeneration Export Rate
Energia currently offers a microgeneration rate of
18.5
cent (18.5c/kWh). Energia’s feed-in tariff stands out for offering a strong return to customers generating renewable electricity through solar PV or other microgeneration methods.
How Payments Work
With Energia's Microgeneration Scheme, you'll receive a credit on your bi-monthly electricity bill for any excess renewable electricity you export to the grid. Thanks to your smart meter, readings are taken every 30 minutes and automatically sent to ESBN.
This exported energy is compensated through the Clean Export Guarantee (CEG) tariff, applied as a credit on your invoice rather than a direct bank transfer. Please note: The export period shown on your bill might sometimes differ from your import period due to ESBN data delivery timings. However, any missed export days will be accounted for on your next bill.
What Smart Plan is best for me?
We have a number of smart plans available for you to choose from.
Find out more here
Who is Eligible?
To join Energia’s Microgeneration Scheme, you must:
Own a microgenerator, such as a solar PV system
Have an export grid connection
Have a smart meter installed (Energia can request one for you)
Submit the NC6 form to ESBN (your installer may do this for you)
Eligible customers may also qualify for financial support via
SEAI grants
to help offset installation costs. Once your export data is shared with Energia by ESBN, you'll begin receiving credits on your electricity bill.
How to Sign Up
Here's how to sign up for Energia’s Microgeneration Scheme:
Own a microgenerator (like solar PV) with an export grid connection.
Ensure your NC6 form is completed and submitted to ESBN. Your installer may have already done this.
Once ESBN processes your form, they notify Energia, and we’ll set up your export account.
Make sure both your electricity import and export are with Energia.
Once ESBN sends us your export data, you'll see payments as a credit on your Energia bill.
The Simple 4-Step Process
1. Install solar panels or another microgenerator
2. Submit your NC6 form and install a smart meter
3. Start exporting surplus electricity to the grid
4. Receive credit on your Energia bill every 2 months
Benefits of Joining Energia’s Scheme
Payment for your surplus energy:
Energia pays you for the excess electricity you export to the grid, currently at a rate of 18.5c per kWh.
Contribute to a greener Ireland:
Exporting your surplus green energy helps Ireland move towards a more sustainable future and reduces your carbon footprint.
Potential tax exemptions:
You may be eligible for a yearly tax exemption of €400 on income earned from selling excess electricity.
Financial support:
Grants from the
Sustainable Energy Authority of Ireland (SEAI)
can help cover installation costs.
Smart Solar bundle:
Energia offers a Smart Solar bundle that provides a saving of €750 on solar panel installation.
No export cap:
If you have a smart meter, there’s no limit to how much electricity you can export.
Trusted by Thousands Across Ireland
Join over 28,000* Energia customers already earning from their microgeneration systems. We’re a trusted supplier of
100% green energy
, committed to helping Ireland transition to a cleaner, more sustainable energy future.
* total number of microgeneration customers as of April 2025
Ready to switch to Energia?
Switch online
View Energy Plans
Call Us
0818 300 701
Request a Call-Back
Contact Us
Energia & The Microgeneration Scheme FAQs
What is Microgeneration and the Microgeneration Scheme?
Microgeneration means producing your own renewable electricity, usually with solar panels (Solar PV). Energia’s
Microgeneration Scheme
lets you earn money by sending any unused electricity back to the grid.
Key points:
You generate clean energy at home.
Any extra electricity you don’t use can be exported to the grid.
Energia pays you for the electricity you export under the scheme.
Am I eligible for the Microgeneration Scheme and the Clean Export Guarantee payment?
Yes, if you meet the following requirements:
Eligibility checklist:
You own a microgenerator, such as a
solar PV system
.
You have an export grid connection.
You have completed and submitted an NC6 form to
ESB
Networks (your installer may have done this for you at the time of installation of the microgenerator.).
What happens next:
Once
ESB
Networks processes your NC6 form, they will notify Energia.
We set up your export account and add payments to your electricity bill based on your export data.
Important for payment:
If you don’t have a smart meter, you’ll need one installed by
ESB
Networks to get paid for your exported electricity.
You can
request a smart meter on the
ESB
Networks website
.
I do not have a Smart Meter but have a Microgeneration installed, am  still eligible?
You’ll need a smart meter to join the Microgeneration Scheme and receive payments for exported electricity.
What to do
Request a smart meter installation from
ESB
Networks.
You can make the
request directly on the
ESB
Networks website
.
I have not received confirmation from Energia that I am eligible for the Microgeneration scheme?
Here’s how the process works and what you can do:
How it works
ESB
Networks sends Energia a notification when your microgeneration installation is registered.
We update your account and email you to confirm we’ve received this information.
If you haven’t heard from us
Make sure your NC6 form and details were submitted correctly to
ESB
Networks.
If everything is complete and you still haven’t received confirmation, please contact Energia for assistance.
I am not an Energia customer, can I still avail of the Microgeneration Scheme?
No, not at the moment. To join the Microgeneration Scheme, your electricity import and export must be with the same supplier.
What to do if you want to join
Sign up with Energia
to avail of the scheme.
Once you’re an Energia customer, we’ll help you set up your export account.
How much will I be paid for the excess energy through the CEG payment?
You’ll be paid 18.5 cent per kWh for exported electricity, credited to your Energia bill.
How will I receive my payment and how often?
Payments are issued as a credit on your bi-monthly electricity bill, not as direct bank transfers.
Will I have a separate account for my Export?
No, your export payments will appear as credits on your existing Energia electricity account.
How will I know how many units I have exported to the Grid?
Your bill will show the export volume based on smart meter readings collected by
ESB Networks
.
Do I get tax back / need to advise of income for taxation?
You may qualify for a tax exemption of up to €400 per year on income from exported electricity. Speak with Revenue or your tax advisor for full details.
How Is deemed export calculated?
Deemed export is an estimated amount of electricity you export when you don’t have a smart meter. This method is less common now because smart meters provide accurate readings.
Good to know
Deemed export is only used if a smart meter isn’t installed.
Smart meters give exact export data, so they’re the preferred option.
What is the difference between metered export and deemed export?
The difference is in how your exported electricity is measured.
Key differences
Metered export uses real-time data from your smart meter, so it’s accurate.
Deemed export is an estimated amount used when smart meter data isn’t available.
How much can I earn from my solar panels?
Your earnings depend on how much excess electricity you export to the grid. With Energia’s current rate of 18.5c per kWh, exporting 1,000 kWh in a year could earn you about €185 in credits.
Good to know
The more electricity you export, the more you earn.
Payments are added as credits to your electricity bill.
Check the
latest Energia rates
for up-to-date information.
What is a feed-in tariff in Ireland?
A feed-in tariff is the payment you receive for surplus electricity exported to the grid. Energia currently pays eligible customers 18.5c/kWh via the Clean Export Guarantee.
Faults & Emergencies
If you are having difficulty with your energy supply or smell gas please call us using our
fault and emergency contact numbers
.

Price Updates
Customer notice
We are increasing our residential Electricity and Gas prices from 12th October 2026.
Please see here for more information.
Energia Price update
What's changing?
From 12th October 2026, changes will apply to residential electricity and gas prices. Below you'll find a summary of the changes and what they mean for Energia customers.
Energia Price Changes
Electricity
customers will see a 4.73% increase to the average annual bill which equates to €1.67 per week. The electricity standing charge will increase by 5% for these customers.
Gas
customers will see a 9.38%
increase to the average annual bill which equates to €2.74 per week. There will be no change to gas standing charges.
Dual Fuel
customers will see a 6.73% increase to the average annual bill which equates to €4.41 per week.
The electricity standing charge will increase by 5% for these customers and there will be no change to gas standing charges.
Full details of changes to our individual rates and specific plans can be found at energia.ie/tariffs
Electricity % increase is based on the Estimated Annual Bill (EAB) for Energia’s Standard Electricity Plan and Energia's Smart Data Plan with typical annual electricity consumption of 4,200 kWh. Gas % increase is based on average annual gas consumption of 11,000 kWh. Inclusive of current Carbon Tax and updated PSO Levy effective 1
st
October 2026.
Why are prices changing?
We don’t take the decision to increase prices lightly and continue to look for ways to keep costs as low as possible for our customers.
However, continued volatility in global energy markets combined with increased network charges means we now need to make some changes to our electricity and gas prices, our first increase in gas since 2022. We fully understand that any changes to pricing affects households and encourage customers who are experiencing difficulties to engage with us for support.
Help, Support & Frequently Asked Questions
What can I do if I’m finding it hard to pay my bills?
If you’re having difficulty paying your bills, we’re here to help.
We collaborate with several charitable and support organisations such as St Vincent de Paul, MABS, Alone, and our customer service team are available to speak to any customers experiencing difficulty.
We have a range of options available for customers.
Please contact us if you have any worries about paying your bill.
How can I save on my electricity costs?
Make sure you are on the right plan for your home. You can check your usage using the Energia Insights app to understand where and when you are using the most energy in your home.
Some homes are better suited to Smart time of use tariffs while others will be more suited to 24 hour plans.
If you don’t think you are on the right tariff, talk to our team about changing to a different plan.
Will my rates change if I am in contract?
Yes. Our tariff rates are variable and are subject to change. This is included in our terms and conditions.
If you are currently on a discounted contract, your prices will be increasing from the 12th October 2026. However, your discount will remain the same and will be deducted from the standard rates applicable to your tariff.
As a result of these changes, you have a right to terminate your contract within the next 30 days. If you would like to discuss your plan, please call us to discuss the best option for you.
Will I be contacted directly about this price change?
We will be contacting customers directly by email to inform them of this change.
Faults & Emergencies
If you are having difficulty with your energy supply or smell gas please call us using our
fault and emergency contact numbers

pages.text: Time of Use Tariff: 5 Reasons to Switch | Energia Skip to main content Search our site CLOSE Home Energy Business Energy Smart Home Store Energia Group Contact Us Search My Account My Account Existing customer offers Energia Rewards How to read your meter Online account management Ways to pay Understanding your bill Energy Plans Electricity Dual Fuel Gas Best Smart Meter plans Switching guide Help me find a plan Home Upgrades All About Smart Meters Electric Vehicle Plans & Chargers Future Homes Hub Deep Retrofit Projects SEAI Grants Solar PV Panels for Homes Microgeneration Scheme Moving Home How to read your meter Landlord account management Help and Support Help and Support Faults and emergencies Vulnerable customers Contact us Energy Wise Gas Boiler Service Business Energy Energia Group Smart Home Store Switch Now Toggle Navigation About Energia Latest news 5 reasons to switch to a time-of-use tariff Table of Contents What are time-of-use tariffs? What are time-of-use tariffs? Benefits of switching to time-of-use tariff Switch to a time-of-use tariff today FAQs: Time-of-Use Tariff Smart Meters July 08 2026 4 min read 5 reasons to switch to a time-of-use tariff If you’re not currently enjoying the financial savings and other benefits of a time-of-use tariff, now is a great time to make the move. Households across Ireland are already reaping the benefits of smart meters through plans that reward them for using electricity at times of lower demand. With a time-of-use tariff, your electricity price changes depending on when you use energy, giving you more control over your bills and helping you make better use of off-peak rates. What are time-of-use tariffs? Time-of-use tariffs are electricity plans that can help you save money by encouraging you to use electricity during off-peak times. Instead of paying the same rates for electricity all day, you pay different rates during day, night and peak periods. This means you can save money by shifting some of your electricity use to cheaper times. At Energia, a time-of-use tariff on a smart meter has the following three time bands: Night (Lowest rate): 11pm - 8am Peak (Highest rate):  5pm - 7pm Day (Moderate rate): 8am-5pm, 7pm-11pm       Benefits of switching to time-of-use tariff There are many advantages of making the switch to a time-of-use tariff. Here are five reasons to consider making the switch. 1. Save money with off-peak rates The top reason for switching to a time-of-use tariff is that it helps you unlock savings on your electricity bills. Day/night/peak plans offer discounted electricity rates at times when there is less demand for electricity. By making simple changes to the way you use electricity, you can easily cut your energy costs. Some of the top ways of achieving this are: Setting appliances for off-peak times: Set your dishwasher, washing machine and other appliances to start their programmes when electricity is cheapest. This will usually mean scheduling them to start when your night rate begins or early in the morning. Batch cooking when electricity is cheaper: Instead of switching on the cooker at peak times when most people are making dinner, batch cook meals when your time-of-use plan offers cheaper electricity price plans . 2. Make EV charging and battery storage more affordable A time-of-use tariff can be especially useful for EV owners and households with battery storage. If you have an electric vehicle, overnight charging can be one of the easiest ways to benefit from cheaper rates. Instead of charging during evening peak hours, you can schedule your EV to charge when electricity demand is lower. At Energia, we also offer discounted EV charging rates between 2am and 6am. 3. Reduce pressure on the electricity grid Switching to a time-of-use tariff does not just benefit your household. It can also help reduce pressure on the wider electricity grid. Electricity demand is usually highest in the early evening, when people return home, cook dinner, use appliances and heat their homes. A time-of-use tariff encourages households to move some usage away from this busy period. When more people shift usage to off-peak times, it can help reduce demand during peak hours, make the grid easier to manage and lower the need for expensive infrastructure upgrades. You can also explore ways to save energy at home in summer , from off-peak appliance use to smarter EV charging. 4. Track and manage your usage Time-of-use tariffs are smart meter plans . This means they give you detailed insights on your electricity use. By tracking your energy usage, you can manage or change how you’re using your electricity. That means no nasty surprises when your bill arrives. Instead, you get detailed insights and the opportunity to take action during your billing cycle. All this data is at your fingertips when you sign up for Energia’s Energy Insights app. You’ll be able to see: Your usage and costs by hour, day, week or month: Check your electricity use over various periods. Easily spot high-usage times and make changes to cut your costs. Track your performance: Set budgets in € for how much you want to spend on electricity. Get at-a-glance graphics showing how you’re doing against your targets. Estimates on energy-guzzling appliances: See which appliances are likely to be using the most energy in your home based on your usage. These insights help you identify appliances that are pushing up your energy bills. You can then change how and when you use them. Comparisons to other households: Track your energy usage against other homes in Ireland. Find out how your electricity use and bills compare to similar households. This can be useful for seeing if you’re doing well or whether there’s room for improvement. Tips on reducing your usage: You’ll find personalised tips and advice on how to cut your electricity usage. These snippets of useful information will guide you towards ways to save on your bills. 5. Support renewable energy Switching to day/night/peak tariffs also has environmental benefits. By shifting your energy use, you're reducing Ireland’s reliance on fossil fuels — and supporting a cleaner grid. Here are a few key ways in which time-of-use tariffs support renewable energy in Ireland: Reducing peak electricity demand: When you move to a time-of-use tariff, you’re helping to ease electricity demand at peak times. This makes it easier to manage demand across the grid. The result is that more of Ireland’s electricity demand can be met using renewable energy instead of fossil fuels. Good for energy bills and good for the environment. With smart meters now in place, Ireland is also moving towards dynamic electricity pricing , where prices can vary more frequently based on real-time renewable generation and grid demand. Maximising solar energy: Many time-of-use plans offer a daytime electricity rate that is cheaper than the peak rate. This encourages electricity use at times when the grid is generating lots of solar power . Make the most of green, sustainable energy provided by the sun during daylight hours. Supporting battery storage: If you have solar panels with battery storage , time-of-use pricing enables you to charge your battery when electricity is less expensive. You can then use your stored battery energy at peak times, when importing from the grid is more expensive. You’ll earn from selling solar power to the grid under our microgeneration scheme. Enjoy financial benefits whether you or someone else uses the cheap solar power you’ve generated. Switch to a time-of-use tariff today Ready to start enjoying all those benefits of a time-of-use tariff? Explore our smart plans and switch to a tariff that helps you find ways to save on your energy bills. Start your switch FAQs: Time-of-Use Tariff What is the time-of-use tariff in Ireland? A time-of-use tariff in Ireland is a smart meter electricity plan where your rate changes depending on whether you use power during day, night or peak hours. What is the cheapest time to use electricity in Ireland? The cheapest time to use electricity in Ireland is usually overnight, often from around 11pm to 8am. Is a time-of-use tariff good for EV owners? Yes, a time-of-use tariff can be useful for EV owners because they can schedule charging during cheaper overnight periods. Energia offers discounted rates between 2am and 6am. What is the cheapest time to run a washing machine? The cheapest time to run a washing machine is usually during your tariff’s off-peak or night-rate period. Powering Your EV Journey: A Guide for New Electric Vehicle Owners
Take a look through our guide for your EV journey.
Congratulations on your new electric vehicle (EV)! You've taken an exciting step toward a greener and more sustainable future. As your trusted energy provider, we're here to support you every step of the way. In this comprehensive guide, we'll walk you through the essential next steps you should take after bringing home your electric vehicle. From charging solutions to energy efficiency tips, we've got you covered.
Selecting the Right Charging Solution
One of the first things to consider as a new EV owner is how and where you'll charge your vehicle. Here are some options to explore:
Home Charging:
Install a Level 2 home charger for fast and convenient charging.
A convenient option is to take advantage of government-funded support to install a
free EV home charger
at your residence. Through this scheme, you can receive a grant of up to €300 towards the purchase and
EV car charger installation at home
, making sustainable transportation both accessible and convenient.. Be sure to take into account the below considerations before making the commitment.
Ensure your home electrical system can handle the load and make any necessary upgrades.
Consider time-of-use (TOU) rates for charging during off-peak hours to save on electricity costs.
Public Charging Stations:
Locate nearby public charging stations using apps and websites designed for EV owners.
Familiarise yourself with different charging connector types (e.g., CCS, CHAdeMO, Tesla Superchargers) and their compatibility with your vehicle.
Understanding Charging Speeds
Charging speed is an essential factor to consider, as it affects how quickly you can get back on the road. Three common levels of charging speed are:
Level 1 (120V):
This is the slowest option and is typically used with a standard household outlet. It's convenient for overnight charging but less suitable for daily use.
Level 2 (240V):
Most home charging stations and many public stations are Level 2 chargers. They offer faster charging speeds, making them ideal for daily charging needs.
DC Fast Charging (Level 3):
These high-speed chargers are typically found at public charging stations and can provide a substantial charge in a short amount of time, perfect for longer trips.
Managing Energy Costs
As an EV owner, you'll need to monitor your energy consumption and costs. Here's how you can do that effectively:
Track Energy Usage:
Keep an eye on your energy consumption by using smart meters or energy monitoring apps. This can help you budget and optimise your charging habits.
Explore Rate Plans:
Your energy provider may offer specific EV rate plans, which can provide cost savings for off-peak charging. Investigate your options and choose the plan that suits your needs.
Solar Power Integration:
Consider generating your electricity with solar panels to offset some or all of your charging costs while reducing your carbon footprint.
Maximising Energy Efficiency
Efficiency is key to making the most of your electric vehicle. Here are some tips for increasing your EV's efficiency:
Plan Your Routes:
Use navigation apps that consider your EV's range and factor in charging stops when planning longer trips.
Drive Efficiently:
Accelerate and brake smoothly, and maintain a steady speed to extend your vehicle's range.
Reduce Energy Drain:
Minimize the use of heating and air conditioning, as these can significantly impact your EV's energy consumption.
Maintenance and Care
Electric vehicles generally require less maintenance than traditional gas-powered vehicles, but some care is still necessary:
Tire Maintenance:
Proper tire inflation can improve your vehicle's efficiency and extend its range.
Battery Care:
Follow the manufacturer's recommendations for battery care, such as avoiding extreme temperatures and charging within specified voltage limits.
Regular Inspections:
Schedule periodic check-ups to ensure your EV's components, including the battery, are in good condition.
Environmental Impact
One of the most significant advantages of owning an electric vehicle is its reduced environmental impact. To make the most of this benefit:
Renewable Energy Sources:
Consider using energy from renewable sources to charge your EV, further reducing your carbon footprint.
Vehicle Recycling:

What is microgeneration?
Microgeneration refers to the generation of electricity from small scale renewable technology such as solar panels.
Think of it as a way to be more self-sufficient!
Solar panels
are generally the most popular choice for micro-generation. In this blog post, we'll dive deeper into what microgeneration is, how it can benefit you, tax exemptions to save you money, and how you can get started with micro-generation.
The benefits of microgeneration
There are several benefits associated with microgeneration.
Energy savings
Microgeneration is like having a little power station right at home.  It’s like growing your own vegetables instead of always buying them from the shop. If you’re eligible for the microgeneration scheme and produce surplus electricity, you will have the option to export this surplus to the grid and receive a payment for it.
Reduced carbon footprint
Microgeneration is also about making a positive impact on the environment. By using renewable energy sources like solar, wind, hydro, or biomass, microgeneration allows individuals to reduce their carbon footprint.
What is the microgeneration scheme?
The microgeneration scheme is a government initiative designed to encourage the generation of renewable energy by households. Under this scheme, individuals can install small-scale renewable energy systems, such as solar panels or hydroelectric systems, to generate electricity or heat for their own use. The microgeneration scheme will allow customers with registered microgeneration installations to sell any excess electricity back to Ireland’s electricity grid in return for the Clean Expert Guarantee (CEG) payment.
Tax exemptions for microgeneration
Individuals who sell their electricity back to the grid in Ireland qualify for tax exemptions. Under the new updated scheme, individuals are eligible for a yearly tax exemption of €400 on the income earned from selling excess electricity.
How does the microgeneration support scheme work?
The microgeneration support scheme supports households and businesses in using renewable energy systems like solar panels and wind turbines. To be eligible for the scheme you must own a microgenerator such as a solar PV system and have an export grid connection. You will also need to complete an NC6 form. Once your form is submitted to ESBN they will notify your energy provider. If you do not have a smart meter at the premises you will need to get one installed by ESB Networks.
If you qualify, you will receive financial support through
grants administered by the Sustainable Energy Authority of Ireland (SEAI)
to help cover installation costs. As mentioned previously, if you produce extra electricity and sell electricity back to the grid, you can receive a payment for it. We currently offer our residential customers a rate of 18.5c per kWh exported to the grid.  Also, regular compliance checks, maintenance, and reporting of energy generation data are necessary to remain eligible for scheme support.
How can I avail of microgeneration?
You can avail of microgeneration in three simple steps.
You must own a microgenerator such as solar PV system and have an export grid connection.
You must notify ESBN that you have installed solar panels by completing the NC6 form. The installer should complete this form on your behalf.
Once the form has been submitted to ESBN, ESBN will send your export usage details to your designated energy provider and payment will show on your electricity bill.
How much can I get for my electricity?
Energia is pleased to offer a rate of 18.5c per kWh to our residential customers. The payment is dependent on the size and type of your microgeneration system, as well as how much surplus electricity you export. You can learn more about
microgeneration rates in Ireland
and how Energia’s export payment works in our dedicated guide.
Export and earn with Energia
Interested in selling electricity back to the grid? With Energia, you can generate your own energy and also reduce the quantity of electricity you import from the electricity grid and lower your carbon footprint. You can also learn more about how Energia supplies
100% green electricity
to homes. Our tailored solution for your solar PV installation can be enhanced with a
smart battery
. With the
smart solar energy bundle
, customers can optimise how they generate, store and use their electricity while reducing reliance on the grid. If you don’t want to sell your excess electricity back to the grid, you can store it in a battery and power your appliances with stored electricity. By partnering with Energia, you gain access to top-notch support and
competitive pricing
.
With our microgeneration plan, you have the opportunity to not only save big, but to also play a pivotal role in driving Ireland’s energy transition. Energia’s commitment to customer satisfaction, combined with our extensive expertise and experience, makes it easy for you to make the right switch.

About Energia
Renewable Electricity
Customer notice
We are increasing our residential Electricity and Gas prices from 12th October 2026.
Please see here for more information.
100% Green Electricity from Energia*
*Subject to verification through the CRU’s Green Source Product Verification process.
All Energia household electricity plans are guaranteed 100% green*. We match the electricity used by our household customers over the course of the year with an equivalent amount of electricity generated from renewable sources.
This is achieved through renewable generation and Guarantees of Origin certificates relating to renewable electricity generated in Ireland and Europe.
Why choose Energia green electricity?
100% renewable electricity*
Every Energia household electricity plan is matched with renewable generation on an annual basis.
Independently verified
Our green electricity products are subject to the CRU’s Green Source Product Verification process.
Renewable generation
Energia generates electricity from wind, solar and other sustainable sources across Ireland.
View Electricity Plans
What this means for our customers
Every year, we work out our household customers’ electricity demand from the national grid. We then match this with an equivalent amount of renewable electricity through our wind farms, solar farms, other renewable generators and Guarantees of Origin certificates.
Electricity from renewable and non-renewable sources is combined on the national grid, so it is not possible to determine the exact source of the electricity used in an individual home at a particular time.
Each
Guarantee of Origin
is an electronic document providing proof that a quantity of energy was produced from renewable sources. The renewable generation and Guarantees of Origin supporting Energia’s green electricity products are reflected in its annual Fuel Mix Disclosure and assessed through the CRU’s Green Source Product Verification process.
Learn more about renewable electricity and its benefits
Where does Energia’s renewable electricity come from?
Energia supplies renewable electricity through a combination of renewable generation in Ireland and Guarantees of Origin certificates relating to renewable generation in Ireland and Europe.
How does Energia invest in renewable energy?
Energia Group is a leading developer and operator of renewable energy and is responsible for
approximately 21% of installed wind power capacity
on the island of Ireland. Energia’s growing renewable energy portfolio consists of 15 onshore wind farm sites, which generate over 300 MW of green electricity, and an additional 900 MW through Power Purchase Agreements.

FAQs about green electricity
What is the Fuel Mix Disclosure and why is it important?
The Fuel Mix Disclosure is a yearly report that shares the mix of fuels energy suppliers provide to customers. It shows the percentage of demand met by each energy source, as well as its CO₂ impact, allowing customers to understand their energy sources and make informed choices about their supplier. The Single Electricity Market Operator calculates it yearly on behalf of the CRU, and the CRU requires it to appear on bills, promotional material and its website.
What is the Green Source Product Verification process?
The Green Source Product Verification Report is an annual CRU report confirming that a supplier’s green source products are 100% renewable. Suppliers submit the total aggregate demand of customers using green source products to SEMO, together with an independent audit, before the CRU publishes the outcome of the verification process.
What is a Guarantee of Origin certificate?
Each Guarantee of Origin certificate, or GoO, verifies that 1 MWh of energy has been generated from a renewable source such as solar, wind or hydropower. They are included under renewable generation in energy suppliers’ Fuel Mix Disclosures.
How do Guarantee of Origin certificates work and are they regulated?
Guarantees of Origin can be sold between European Economic Area states under EU legislation. Their buying and selling are regulated by the CRU and the Irish and EU markets to support fairness and transparency, ensure the certificates represent verified green energy and prevent double counting. Read through the CRU’s website to see the process for regulating green energy claims
here
.
Am I guaranteed 100% Renewable Electricity at a specific time?
The electricity grid combines renewable and non-renewable electricity, so it is impossible to know whether the electricity used in your home at a particular moment came from wind, solar or another source. Energia instead works out your annual electricity demand from the grid and matches it with an equal amount of renewable energy, as reflected in its yearly Fuel Mix Disclosure and Green Source Product Verification process.
Does Energia supply 100% renewable electricity and how do I know my plan is green?
Energia matches its customers’ electricity demand with 100% renewable generation on an annual basis. All Energia household electricity plans are 100% green and are supported by renewable generation in Ireland and Guarantees of Origin certificates relating to renewable generation in Ireland and Europe.
What does green electricity mean?
Green electricity generally refers to electricity backed by renewable sources such as wind, solar and hydropower. For Energia household plans, customers’ annual electricity demand is matched with an equivalent amount of renewable electricity through renewable generation and Guarantees of Origin, subject to the CRU’s verification process.
How much of Ireland’s electricity comes from renewable sources?
Renewable sources accounted for 40.9% of Ireland’s electricity supply in 2025, based on provisional SEAI estimates. Ireland is working towards a target of generating 80% of its electricity from renewable sources by 2030.
What is renewable electricity?
Renewable electricity is electricity generated from sources that naturally replenish, such as wind, sunlight and water. It is one form of renewable energy, which can also include renewable heating and fuels.
